title: The 1 Billion Views Content Strategy Every App Should Steal in 2026
summary: Dawson Gibbs posted daily for about six years before going viral, became one of Cal AI's first influencers (about 200M views across his page and Cal AI's), then founded UGC agency Evo Marketing. His rule is to match the creator to the purchase: credible experts (an ex-flight attendant for flight-deal app Jetpack) for considered buys, relatable peers for impulse buys. A campaign for business marketplace SMB Market drove 40M views and about $1.2M but roughly 45% churn, fixed by switching from 20-year-old 'get rich quick' creators to 35-40-year-olds. Videos at 10-20k views with at least 3% engagement get reposted until one breaks out.

title: How To Grow Your App 23x Faster Than The Competition
summary: Canyon, a SideShift co-founder, explains how to staff a creator program: in the discovery phase the key role is a strategist who reviews every video before it posts, at scale it is the recruiter, and a first generalist manager costs about $2-4k a month plus about 5% of creator bonuses. Over the prior 3-6 months Instagram delivered roughly 10-20% more views than TikTok at similar volume, while TikTok shadowbans money-making niches. Ultra-narrow niches convert well but cap near $10k a month unless you expand to adjacent audiences; a US creator costs about $25 a video versus about $15 in LATAM. SideShift sells creator-marketplace access, so read accordingly.

title: 1,000 Hours of Studying The Most Profitable Apps in 17 Minutes
summary: Joseph Choi, the show's host and Consumer Club founder, condenses his founder interviews into one monologue. His margin math: paid ads typically run at 10-30% margin and mass organic UGC at about 50%, but organic has a natural ceiling of roughly $1-3M a year per app from TikTok and Reels, after which proven organic videos and creators should feed paid ads. He frames content strategy as three layers (copy a format, iterate one variable, or transplant a whole concept into your niche, as Pingo did) run by three separate roles: social-growth lead, creator manager/coach and talent scout. All numbers are his heuristics or secondhand, and the video ends in a Consumer Club pitch.

title: The NEW App Content Strategy Dominating in 2026
summary: Matt Espinoza runs Clover Labs, an agency whose own revenue he puts at $0 to $8M a year in six months and whose clients get about 250M views a month. The method is industrial cloning: about 90% of a campaign is tweaked copies of proven posts and 10% experiments; a median clone gets about 20% of the original's views, so 5-10 clones match it. Translating and dubbing winners adds roughly 20% views per new country (his rule of thumb). He also seeds Reddit posts and comments that AI chatbots cite, partly through subreddits Clover owns, which breaks Reddit's rules; all figures are agency-reported.

title: How to Build an $18M/Year Apple Watch App (FREE MASTERCLASS)
summary: Welltory reads Apple Watch data to show you what is draining your energy: $18M ARR, nearly 18M downloads. CPO Assia Poloni opens the internal deck. The first onboarding CTA asks users to sync health data before they see anything else, and over 90% say yes. The most persuasive proof is not social proof, it is the user's own data.

title: Meet The Marketing Genius Behind Cal AI
summary: Two years ago Alfie Dickens was fixing stadium chairs. He talked his way into a two-week trial and built Cal AI's entire influencer machine, running at $60M/year at peak. The scale is brute force: 25 assistants, 100 cold emails each per day, ~2,000 daily, 220,000+ influencers contacted to sign a few thousand. Covers minimum-view clauses, the seven-touch rule, and the 15-second rule.

title: #1 UGC EXPERT Reveals How To Market Consumer Apps
summary: Nick Lawson co-founded SideShift, where most well-known apps run their UGC campaigns, so he sees conversion data across hundreds of campaigns. His counterintuitive finding: AI-made UGC gets views but does not convert. The teams that win split budget 20% making content, 80% putting spend behind the videos that already worked.

title: $16M AI CEOs: How to Make $1.3M/Month With AI Apps
topics: Buy / Sell / Exit, Paid Ads, Paywall & Pricing
summary: Patrick runs Social, a 22-app studio with 40M downloads and $16M annual revenue, once hitting $11M with exactly 11 people. They both build and buy apps, and ship 4,000 AI-made video ads a month. Their most surprising win: removing the paywall from the Celebs onboarding entirely.

title: Beginners Guide to Buying & Selling Apps 2026
topics: Buy / Sell / Exit, Growth & ASO, Paywall & Pricing
summary: Steve Young (App Masters) builds and buys apps around App Store search: find a keyword with roughly 30+ search volume and weak competition, then name the app after it, since title and subtitle are '80% of ASO'. A 2022 acquisition went from $1-2k to $8-10k a month on the same 100-150 daily downloads after a hard paywall and a $60/year price (trial starts 6% to 13%); an app bought in March 2024 has made over $1M lifetime, mostly from App Store search. He walks through debt-financed purchases with illustrative loan math and wants at least a $3 RPI before trying Meta ads.

title: $172M of App Building Advice in 50 Minutes
topics: Buy / Sell / Exit, Paywall & Pricing, Growth & ASO
summary: Josh runs M&A at Blue Throne, which buys consumer apps doing $400k-$15M a year. Growth stories sell for about 6x run-rate revenue at best, and he gives buyer thresholds: year-one resubscribe of 50% is amazing and 20% bad; an organic install share of 50%+ is great, under 20% a paid-ads treadmill. His pricing argument is that ChatGPT reset consumer price expectations from about $60 a year to $20 a month; his Waking Up example (about 25k downloads a month but over $1M a month in revenue) is his own Sensor Tower estimate.

title: I speedran an ai app to $100k in 70 days.
topics: UGC & Content, Paywall & Pricing, Growth & ASO
summary: Cedric took Pep AI to $100k in 70 days by studying successful GLP/peptide apps and doing the opposite. They ran ads only, so he signed every creator in the peptide niche instead. Month one $30k, month two $50k, month three tracking to $80k. A $200/month retainer for roughly 20,000 views is his low-risk test unit.

title: How to Build a $2M/Month App (Copy Me)
summary: Marcus Burke has run Meta ads for apps for 14 years, scaled one app to $2M/month, and has a single creative that spent over $1M. The key point: app ads are not e-commerce ads. You have to prime the viewer that they are about to enter the App Store or install rate collapses. He walks through his Reddit research pipeline paired with Claude for copy.

title: The 14-Year-Old Who Built a $14k/Month AI App
summary: Evan Yadegari is in 9th grade and took his app Locked past $14k/month, then hit $30k ARR in the first 30 days with 10X. He is the younger brother of Cal AI's founder but did not copy him; he tested Reddit, X, influencers and paid ads himself to find which channel actually moved installs. The deepest section covers four influencer deal structures and how to write minimum-view terms.

title: I Studied 1,000,000 UGC Ads, This Is What Will Grow  Your App
summary: Drew Levin at SideShift sees which content is driving hundreds of millions of views for apps. One counterintuitive call: if you build an AI product, lean into the fact that people hate AI, the way Suno lets its comment section rage and feeds on the watch time. He also separates the Creator Manager role (logistics) from the Content Coach role (creative notes), with the manager-to-creator ratios that hold up at scale.

title: The EXACT System to Go From 0-$10M+ With Your App
summary: StudyFetch has 7M+ users after 2.5 years, seven-figure MRR, eight-figure ARR and 2B+ views. They bootstrapped 18 months on TikTok alone. Their first video hit 3M views overnight and brought in tens of thousands of signups, and only then did they raise an $11.5M Series A with the College Board participating. Kieran breaks down three creator strategies, including using zero-follower accounts with premium influencers.

title: The NEW Short Form Strategy Dominating For App Growth
summary: Yannis is a machine learning scientist, not a marketer, and he reached 300M views and 3-5M downloads without hiring a single creator. Instead he opens 50-100 fresh TikTok accounts a week and produces everything in-house, keeping full creative control. He uses SpyTok to correlate view counts against App Store rank, and separates format from content when researching.

title: she makes $400k/mo from ai apps (while in college)
summary: Nicole built four apps before 25; her two most recent clear over $400k/month combined. GlamUp reached 1M users in six months and peaked at $150k MRR; Sprout hit $250k MRR in eight months on 100M monthly views. She started from her bedroom with no technical background. One copycat app made $100k in a week; tripling price and one paywall test added 50% conversion.

title: I speedran a new app from 0 to $2m/year in 6 months (here's how)
topics: Paywall & Pricing, UGC & Content, Paid Ads
summary: Daniel took a dating-profile analysis app from zero to $2M ARR in six months, but the lesson is that he built distribution before writing a line of code, selling $15 manual profile reviews on Instagram. By launch he already had thousands of paying customers. His TikTok slideshow system produces a month of content in under two hours, and switching the paywall default to annual doubled revenue per user.

title: Copy This Facebook Ads Strategy, It'll Blow Up Your App
topics: Paid Ads, UGC & Content, Buy / Sell / Exit
summary: Alex grew Boost App Social, an Instagram hashtag and growth tool, to about $100k MRR almost entirely on Meta ads, then sold it for seven figures in January 2026. Of the $1.5-1.8M he spent on Meta, about $800k was wasted, and roughly 1 in 85 video creatives ended up taking the spend, so the operation is built around creative volume. Creators were sourced from about 1,000 Gmail accounts sending around 10 emails each, and he held 200-300 UGC videos under perpetual-rights contracts.

title: How I built a $500k/mo ai app (so you can just copy me)
summary: Mori's language app Pingo hit nearly 400M views in 30 days and is approaching $500k monthly revenue, 14 months after starting from a dorm room. His principle is meaningfully viral: every video from all 100 creators must show the product, no cheap view-bait. The breakout format is Pingo insulting users until they cry, at 52M views.

title: COPY this ai app's $6.7m/yr marketing strategy
summary: Brett and Zack built Coconote, an AI note-taking app for students: $100k ARR in 45 days, $1M in four months, $6.7M ARR and 2M signups a year later. They refuse to chase raw views, preferring 10M on-target views over 40M scattered ones. Their team is 10-12 part-time creators who understand the product, what they call Navy SEALs rather than the Navy. Quizlet acquired them.

title: 0 to $300k/mo in 45 days with my ai app (just copy me)
summary: Dillion ran out of money after 18 months on a failed product. One creator's TikTok returned 6:1 ROI, so he took a $100k personal loan and put all of it into creators. 85 creators, 300 posts a day, 600M views in 60 days, and Halo AI reached $300k MRR in 45 days.

title: I speedran an ai app from 0 to $1m/yr in 10 months
summary: Kobe Conrad took sobriety app Sunflower to $1M ARR in 10 months with a move most founders never consider. Instead of hiring 30 micro-influencers and measuring CPM, he found the single biggest influencer in the sobriety space and hired them outright as VP of Sobriety. That one person generates 50-100M views a month and drives 50-100k clicks to the app.

title: The Stupid Simple Content Strategy That's Making Apps Go Viral
summary: Casper sits on the other side of the table: he is the creator apps hire, so he sees which formats land and which flop before anyone else does. He turned those formats into his own apps, making $217k in five months. His counterintuitive rule: never say the app name out loud in the video. Short-form content kept driving installs past day 500.

title: I speedran an ai app from 0 to $100k exit in 26 days
topics: Buy / Sell / Exit, UGC & Content, Build & No-Code
summary: Caleb Dean sold his running app Runafy after about 26 days of revenue: the buyer estimated MRR at around $3k and paid roughly 4.5-5x ARR, with Caleb keeping 30% equity and a six-month earnout. He validated with fewer than 50 copied Instagram Reels (a 2,000-person waitlist, 90+ paid $5), posted nine Reels a day, and used App Store pre-orders to get 3,000 downloads at launch. The deal started with a cold X DM. He also covers his first app, a no-code paruresis app whose niche search traffic converted at 30%+.

title: Meet The 18y/o Who Solved UGC Marketing (100M Views in 2 Weeks)
summary: Driss is 18 and is the person actually behind Cluely's UGC program, 100M views in two weeks. Before that he dropshipped fake AirPods on TikTok, which is where he trained his sense for what goes viral. His method: gamify content production with a $40 bonus for a creator's first video, and a belief that 20 consistent creators beat 2,000 unmanaged ones.

title: Copy This UGC Strategy, It'll Make Your App Go Viral
summary: Jay runs travel app Nomad Table solo but manages 60 creators, generating 44M views and $65k revenue a month with over 1M downloads and no funding. The only metric he trusts is watch time past the 3-second mark, with a 75-80% threshold. He still creates as a top creator himself to act as a quality filter, and pays creators at a $1-2 CPM.

title: Full App Growth Guide 2026 - How to Make Viral Content to Get Users & Make Your App Retentive
summary: An, founder of couples app Flame, took day-30 retention from 0.8% (his earlier date planner Sparks) and 4.2% (Flame AI, a ChatGPT wrapper) to about 50% in roughly eight months with a daily couples question, streaks, widgets and carrot-and-stick notifications. Distribution is a TikTok farm of 20-30 in-house accounts on about 10 iPhones posting AI slideshows and memes: 50M views and about 150k users, all organic. He shares view-to-download rates by format (0.05-0.2% for memes and slideshows, 0.5-1% when the app is shown in use) and his VSC filter (Viral, Scalable, Convertible); no revenue is disclosed.

title: I made 4,000 app paywalls and learned this
summary: Jonathan Parra, Superwall's lead paywall designer, has designed over 4,000 paywalls (he says closer to 4,500). He entered the field believing there was a golden paywall you could copy anywhere, and he was wrong. Findings: a simpler paywall with less copy and no comparison table beat a more descriptive one by 111% (both used a plain Continue button, so it was not a button test); single-page bullet-list paywalls are one of the few designs that work across almost every category; and price-and-packaging design is one of the biggest levers to test. Superwall sponsors the show.

title: this 14 yr old makes $100k/mo PROFIT building apps with ai (here's how)
summary: Raphael Kramer has turned viral memes into apps more than 50 times. At 14 he stayed up one night building a game from the DaBaby meme, shipped it to the App Store and promoted it through his own few-hundred-thousand-follower account: six figures of profit in one month and around 2M downloads. He finds ideas in TikTok comment sections and uses sunk-cost psychology in onboarding.

title: Meet The Guy Who Solved App Growth on TikTok
summary: Founders on Nick Weber's Noise platform generated over 2.5B views in a year, and he treats that as science rather than luck. It started with what he calls eggs theory: small details that look random are the line between 1,000 views and 10M. He built a system where 50,000 people post simultaneously to test those details at scale.

title: Meet The Guy Dominating The App Store
summary: Ryan built a portfolio of roughly 30 apps with 50M+ downloads, including one that was the most-downloaded app in the US for a day, ahead of TikTok and Google. The interesting part is that even with the factory running, they still cannot explain why one creator repeatedly hits tens of millions of views (66.9M on a single video) while cloning that exact video across 20-40 other creators does nothing.

title: The App Marketing Strategy No One Talks About
summary: Nick and Ivan grew not through content but through comments: one campaign left 300,000 comments on Instagram and drove 7,000 clicks. Behind it is not a hundred staff but an automated phone farm; they wrote their own Android build so every account gets its own device, scaling toward 1,000 units. Blunt comments that openly admit to being an app convert best.

title: he had nothing.. until he built a stupid simple $30k/mo app with AI
summary: Dimitri ground for 2.5 years on almost nothing: six months before charging anything, another year to reach $1,000, the year after to $10k, then $28k. He got press on Fox, CNBC, Wired and the Washington Post, and none of it brought users. What it left behind was domain authority, and SEO turned out to be the real growth engine. Covers painkillers versus vitamins and why dating is profitable.

title: He Went From Struggling to Make $1 From His App to Turning Down $1M
summary: Jack Frics built four apps: one took eight months to earn its first dollar then jumped to $15k in a month, one was offered $1M and he turned it down, and the latest hit 100k downloads in 10 weeks. He is not a strong developer or a growth expert. He scrolls TikTok for an hour each morning, finds the format that is working, and remakes it 400 times.

title: This 23 Yr Old Genius Makes $1M/Year with No-Code Apps. Here's How
summary: Connor is 23 and earns over $1M a year; his app Payout alone brings in $45k a month, almost entirely from influencers, and he pays them nothing. He gives equity, then builds apps specifically for each person's audience. It inverts the incentive: creators want the app to last rather than just clear a post.

title: How I Built the #1 App on The App Store (Twice)
summary: Roger Chen took two social apps to #1 on the App Store. Lobby reached 500k daily users and #1 in five countries with no ad spend; Bro, an AI companion that lives on your lock screen, hit #1 in the US off TikTok. He tests ideas by filming Protopie mockups as video before the app is close to finished.

title: How I make $42k/mo passively with simple no-code apps (copy me)
topics: Build & No-Code, UGC & Content, Growth & ASO
summary: Kyle Fowler made $700k from two trading-card scanner apps he built in school, now around $41k MRR after two years running near-passively at $10k a month. Launch day brought 12 downloads from one Reddit post. The real weapon was ASO: two weeks of keyword research held the #1 rank for two years on zero ad spend. When he lost the rank in May 2024 he moved to TikTok.

title: Our app makes $750k/mo thanks to this UGC strategy
summary: Matt vibe-coded a startup over 11 months, had never posted on TikTok, and his first video went viral. Five months later Jenni AI acquired him through an Instagram DM. He now runs Jenni's UGC program: 75M views, 150 creators, under $2 per 1,000 views. He ignores follower count and looks for what he calls camera charisma, recruiting creators from completely unrelated niches.

title: He went from 0 to $150k by building an ai fashion app (no-code)
topics: UGC & Content, Growth & ASO, Build & No-Code
summary: Reed Moncada built Fitted, an AI wardrobe app, to 500M+ views and 600k downloads. The playbook: find creators with 1-50k followers who have viral potential but are not expensive yet, pay $20 a video to test, and when one works bring them on as a co-founder with real equity. Co-founder Max went from filming outfit videos in class to driving half a billion views.

title: Our No-Code Apps Made $50M Using THIS Paywall
summary: Vah Bagdasarian has run over 10,000 paywall experiments and added more than $50M in revenue across apps including Cal AI. His specialty is looking at an app that appears healthy and naming exactly how much money it is leaving on the table, for example moving install-to-paid from 1.1% to around 4%. Multi-step paywalls typically beat single screens by 20-40%.

title: this ai study app makes $100k/mo. here's how (no-code)
summary: Julian Alvarez, technical co-founder of AI study app Jungle, runs it at $80-100k a month. His advice cuts against engineering instinct: spend two weeks on distribution only before touching the product; if nothing happens, probably nobody needs it. One micro-influencer video took MRR from about $2k to about $15k in one to two weeks, but for a stretch influencer spend exceeded what came back. Today about 30 in-house creators post roughly 400 videos a week at about $2 CPM, and 30-40% of new users arrive by word of mouth.

title: He made $2.2M from building simple apps. Here's how (no-code)
summary: Dan Kwan turns cultural trends into apps: Conch AI made $500k from a single viral video, an anime fitness app does $50k a month, and a Duolingo-style Bible app hit $75k MRR in 14 days. Around 220M views total. He explains how to spot a wave before it peaks and his Frankenstein technique for viral content.

title: Copy This Growth Strategy, It'll Blow Up Your App
summary: Phoenix Do builds manifesting and self-help apps, now at $25k MRR on 100k downloads. He once impersonated the Astronomer CEO's daughter to promote an app, pulling 50M views in a week. The more useful part is the funnel detail: extending onboarding with social proof, video and a few questions doubled conversion. Goes deep on when to use a hard paywall versus a free trial.

title: Our App Makes $30K/Month Profit Using This Simple Strategy (copy us)
summary: Alejandro and Mario make about $30k a month in profit from PushScroll (do push-ups to earn scrolling time), entirely organically. Alejandro posted a concept video for an app that did not exist; when it blew up he found Mario on YC co-founder matching and they shipped an MVP in about two weeks. The launch video (about 175k views, with a free-lifetime offer) brought about 20k downloads; a ManyChat comment funnel and an onboarding rewrite (conversion about 7% to 16%) followed, and a 3-4k-member Discord votes on features.

title: How to Make Viral Content 100% Using AI in 2025
summary: Zuhair Lani runs a phone farm posting AI content to TikTok accounts: one client hit 4.7M views from just 15 accounts in under four weeks, and he once made over $100k in a month from fully AI content. His stated rule is that AI does 95% and a human has to fix the last 5%, and he refuses to sell full automation as a dream. Raised $1M from a16z.

title: He Built a Simple $120k/Yr App, Then Sold It For Multiple 6 Figures!
summary: PrayScreen makes you pray before unlocking your phone. It reached about $120k ARR in five to six months, with 60% day-30 retention and US installs at $0.39-0.80 from Meta ads that reused the winning TikTok creative. He tweeted about it and sold it within about a week (later he says three days), his fourth exit. His selling rule: 90%+ of deals fall through, so take the third-highest offer if that buyer can close in four to five days.

title: This 20yr old girl is a marketing genius…
summary: Eunice Lie went from student to CMO at startup Series, generating over 3M impressions across LinkedIn and Twitter; one LinkedIn post produced around 2,500 job applications. Her principle is simple: do the opposite of what everyone else is doing, and build an actual character archetype people can follow.

title: I Built a $30k/mo App That Helps You Quit Smoking
summary: Asher and Thatcher run Clear 30, an app for quitting or cutting back on weed (cannabis, not tobacco), and took it from $10k to $30k a month in about two months through paid social ads plus onboarding and paywall testing. Changing only the first paywall screen moved conversion from about 18-19% to about 30%. A rating prompt added before the reviews screen took App Store ratings from about 50 to about 1,000.

title: My App Makes $600k/Year Using This Easy Growth Strategy (copy me)
summary: Three engineers built workout tracker Stronger from a basement to about 1.2M users and roughly $600k ARR. Their engine is one roughly 6-second Instagram 'fade-in' format they keep reposting, which Peter estimates at 150-200M views (maybe 300M, including one 100M-view month); the intro's '300 times' and '300M+ views' are narration. They openly say they are not marketers, and admit viewers often do not realize it is a workout app from the screenshot.

title: This app makes $2m/year using this ridiculously easy strategy
summary: Dan built Massive, an app that uses GPT to fill out job applications, now at $2M ARR, and he hated the idea when he first heard it. He posted it on LinkedIn as a test and it exploded. His blunt position: waitlists are useless, charge people from day one. It is harder, and the signal is real.

title: Meet The Guy Who Solved Growing Apps (Hunter Isaacson Interview)
topics: Growth & ASO, Paid Ads, Paywall & Pricing
summary: Hunter Isaacson built NGL, the anonymous Q&A app that rides Instagram story links, to 150M MAU and what he calls multi-eight-figure yearly revenue from $1-7 weekly subscriptions priced by country; his earlier app Wink had 70M downloads. NGL sat flat for six months after a one-month build until one TikTok broke it. The practical stretch: how an app at $10k MRR should spend a growth budget (the host raises it to $20k a month) - many small creative tests tracked by cohort, paired with product-led invites.

title: The Secret Behind Weirdly Viral Apps
summary: Canyon co-founded SideShift, a platform where 150,000 college students take UGC work and film daily. This is the high-volume organic playbook: hire students, ship consistently, find the format that converts. He opens up the actual accounts and case studies driving installs at the time of recording.

title: This App Makes $2M/Year With This Viral TikTok Strategy
summary: The CEO of Bloom, a fintech app with several million in ARR and over a million active users, describes the growth loop: test creative with organic creators first, then take the winning assets into paid ads so you spend less budget. Covers scaling from one creator to 5, 10, then 20 micro influencers. He also argues most people underrate product-market fit and pour everything into marketing.

title: How I Grow Viral Apps to 1M+ Downloads (just copy me)
summary: Yev is head of growth at edtech app Sizzle, and before that took faceless YouTube Shorts channels to billions of views. His approach is finding the tipping point rather than collecting scattered growth hacks. The most valuable part is how he segments data so cost per purchase does not lead to the wrong decision, and how he balances organic against paid.

title: The Secrets of Consumer Club: Insights from Joseph Choi - Superwall Podcast
summary: Joseph Choi founded Consumer Club, the Discord where top consumer app founders trade notes on what is currently working. He came up as an internet marketer through e-commerce and affiliate, so he sees everything through a distribution lens. The longest episode on the channel, covering how to convert attention into downloads and the role the comment section plays in conversion.
